newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares close sharply higher.

text.p: Turkish stocks rose sharply on Wednesday when the central bank and the treasury said in a joint protocol that lowering chronic inflation was a priority, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 ended 2.54 percent or 53 points higher at 1,903.

The seven-point protocol was signed by treasury undersecretary Mahfi Egilmez and central bank governor Gazi Ercel, who restated their aims to keep inflation, currently just under 80 percent, below 90 percent.
At the signing ceremony, Egilmez said he expected inflation to decline in 1998 after measures taken in the latter part of this year.
State shares, especially iron and steel producer Eregli and Turkish Airlines led market activity, dealers said.
"Eregli was the leader of the market with a share of more than 11 percent in the total volume. It gained 9.3 percent," said Ilker Ardal from Inter Securities.
An Ankara administrative court said on Tuesday it had cancelled the tender for the partial block sale of Eregli, because it was against the constitution.
Mustafa Yilmaz, head of Mustafa Yilmaz Securities, said the court cancellation did not continue to put Eregli shares under pressure on Wednesday.
"No one indeed believed that Eregli would be privatised soon," he said.
Brokers say the government is expected to continue its efforts to privatise Eregli later this year and next year.
Strong buy orders for Eregli from a large private bank accelarated the uptrend on the exchange, brokers said.
"Other state shares were strong too," said Ilker Ardal. "However overnight rates are still high and they are seen as an attractive investment alternative to the bourse."

Of the 249 shares traded, gainers outdid losers sharply by 152 to 53 and 44 were stable. The IMKB Industrial .XUSIN jumped 3.11 percent to 1,858, the IMKB Services .XUHIZ gained 2.87 percent to 1,901 and the IMKB Financial .XUMAL up by 1.66 percent to 2,017.
The highest rises were seen in the index representing the metals sector with a sharp 6.46 percent gain.
Leading active share of the session was largely state owned flat steel producer Eregli up 2,000 to 23,500, followed by Turkish Airlines, up 1,500 to 50,000 and Yapi Kredi Bank, up 50 lira to 3,600.
The three made up 21.5 percent of the total volume.
